title: August and the Drop
premise: Bram Okafor, a witness-protection investigator who once laundered her own identity into a new life, discovers her safe house listed online — the listing uploaded by someone who knows exactly who she is. As she traces the leak, she uncovers a slush fund moving through three governments ahead of a financial-crimes summit, and realizes her testimony from twelve years ago is the loose end an assassin named Vess has been hired to tie off. Forced out of hiding, Bram allies with the one person she should never trust — the summit's own compliance chief, Elias, whose duty and growing love for her pull in opposite directions. In the end, Bram chooses exposure over survival, delivering the evidence at the summit as Vess closes in; she survives, but only by sacrificing the anonymity that was her whole life, walking out of the hall into a world that finally knows her name.
about_author: C. M. Winterbourne is the pen name of a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing money across borders before turning to fiction full-time. They write thrillers from a small coastal town, drawing on real-world financial forensics and a lifelong fascination with people who reinvent themselves.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: POV: Bram. Scrolling property listings out of habit, Bram freezes on photos of her own safe house — her kettle, her books, her view — listed by a brokerage that doesn't exist. The emotional beat is cold dread: twelve years of invisibility ending in a single webpage. She reports it internally and is told to stay put, which is exactly what she cannot do.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: POV: Bram, with a flashback to her original testimony twelve years ago. We learn how she became a witness, what she saw, and why her handler, Marsh, rewrites the rules to keep her contained. The emotional beat is resentment curdling into resolve as Bram realizes the listing wasn't a mistake — it was a message.

chapters.title: Three Flags
chapters.summary: POV: Elias. The summit's compliance chief notices the same transaction pattern Bram once flagged, now resurrected in a shell network spanning three jurisdictions. His duty says report it; his instinct says someone inside wants it buried. The emotional beat is quiet alarm — a professional realizing the system he serves is the crime scene.

chapters.title: The Broker Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: POV: Bram. She traces the listing to a dead man's identity and a real-estate office that closed years ago, finding a hidden camera feed still live inside her walls. The emotional beat is violation and fury; she stops being prey and starts hunting, burning her own cover to follow the wire.

chapters.title: Found Family
chapters.summary: POV: Bram and Elias alternating. Bram, exposed, reaches out to the two other protected witnesses from her original case — Dee and Okonkwo, her makeshift family of survivors. The emotional beat is warmth under threat: for one night they are a family again, and Bram understands what she's actually fighting to keep.

chapters.title: Vess
chapters.summary: POV: the assassin, briefly, then Bram. Vess arrives in the city, patient and professional, eliminating a middleman who knew too much. Bram realizes the listing was bait to flush her toward a kill zone before the summit. The emotional beat is terror sharpened into clarity: she has four days.

chapters.title: The Rewritten Rule
chapters.summary: POV: Bram and Elias meeting for the first time, each suspecting the other. They trade half-truths over encrypted coffee, then choose trust — Elias hands her the fund's ledger fragment, Bram hands him her old testimony. The emotional beat is the first spark of love against duty, two people breaking their own rules.

chapters.title: Safe House Burning
chapters.summary: POV: Bram. Vess finds Dee and Okonkwo; Bram gets Dee out, but Okonkwo is taken, and the safe house burns as a signature. Marsh offers Bram extraction and silence — the old bargain — and she refuses. The emotional beat is grief weaponized: survival is no longer the goal, truth is.

chapters.title: The Summit Floor
chapters.summary: POV: Bram and Elias. On the summit's opening day, Bram walks in under Elias's credentials, the full ledger assembled, while Vess hunts the building and Marsh's people try to contain the leak. The emotional beat is breathless ascent — every door a coin flip, every guard a question of whose side duty is on.

chapters.title: August and the Drop
chapters.summary: POV: Bram. In the plenary hall, Bram delivers the evidence live as Vess closes in; Elias chooses her over his career, and Marsh chooses the institution and pays for it. Okonkwo is recovered, Vess is taken, and Bram walks out into the open, name known, family intact. The emotional beat is costly peace: she bought the truth with the only currency she had left.
